Bitwarden is the trusted identity security leader for millions of users worldwide, empowering enterprises, developers, and individuals to securely manage and share sensitive information anywhere. As a Senior Software Engineer on Bitwarden's Secrets Manager team, you will build and operate the application stack that lets developers, DevOps, and cybersecurity teams centrally store, manage, and deploy sensitive credentials. This is a **hands-on role**. You will spend your time writing, reviewing, and shipping code within core concepts of secrets, projects, machine accounts, and access tokens across the product suite.

Secrets Manager spans a .***NET API, a Rust SDK core, and a TypeScript and Angular web client,*** with SDK bindings in eight further languages and integrations written in Go, C++, Java, PHP and Python. You should be comfortable moving between languages and learning new ones as the work demands, developing deep expertise as you go.

* **Engineering Standards and Automated Quality:** Review your teammates' pull requests with care and invite the same scrutiny of your own. Pair on hard problems, share what you learn, and help newer engineers find their footing in a security-sensitive codebase.
* **Decoupled Architecture and Service Boundaries:** Maintain clean service boundaries and design resilient APIs so Secrets Manager can evolve independently of the core platform.
* **Deep Technical Work & Codebase Health:** Take on the hardest problems in the codebase. Contribute to performance, reliability, accessibility, architecture and maintainability.
* **AI-Assisted Development:** Use AI coding assistants effectively in daily engineering, and exercise judgement about where they help and where they do not.
* **Operational Stewardship:** Own the operational health, performance, and reliability telemetry of your services in production.
* **Cross-Functional Partnership & Collaboration:** Partner closely with Product, Design, Security, and the other team's engineers to design and validate solutions before implementation begins.

**WHAT YOU BRING TO BITWARDEN**

* **Overall Experience:** 5+ years building and operating production software, with a track record of owning substantial, technically demanding features end to end as an individual contributor.
* **Technical Stack - Expertise:**

  + Languages such as Rust, Go, and Python
  + Tooling such as Terraform, Ansible, and GitHub Actions
  + Containerized environments such as Kubernetes
  + Writing, consuming, and using SDKs / APIs
* **Technical Stack - Experience**:

  + C# / .NET
  + TypeScript / Angular
  + Entity Framework with implementations of Postgres, MySQL, and SQLite
* **Technical Stack - Familiarity:**

  + Languages such as C++, Java, PHP
  + WASM instruction format
* **T-Shaped Engineering Mindset:** Practical experience with containerized environments (Docker/Kubernetes), automated test frameworks (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and SRE/observability tools (APM, alerting, and telemetry dashboards).
* **Secure Coding:** Familiarity with zero-trust and zero-knowledge security architectures, encryption standards, and threat-modeling methodologies.

* **Collaborative Spirit:** A highly collaborative and adaptable mindset, excited to work in rapid, outcome-driven feedback loops.
* **Open Source Passion:** Excitement and enthusiasm for open source, developer advocacy, and building a more secure internet.
* **Problem-Solving:** Excellent problem-solving skills, valuing written, clear documentation and using data to make technical decisions.

* Become an expert. You'll get immersed in the prominent technology markets of security and open source software.

This range acknowledges the strong expertise and significant contributions expected at this level. This is a fully remote role. We believe the best engineers can do world-class work from anywhere, and we hire accordingly. Work from where you do your best work.

**About the Role:**

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through.

This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery.

You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust — your platform is what their work composes with.

At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own.

**What You'll Do:**

* Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones.
* Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability — so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it.
* Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners finding system-of-record tickets metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering.
* Own delivery of the security gates — SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery.
* Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers — tooling other engineers actually adopt.
* Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop — reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations.
* Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own.
* Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own.

**What We Look For:**

* 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience.
* Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days.
* Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python.
* Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure.
* Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling — jobs, shared templates, runners — GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus.
* Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code — able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring.
* Hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning tooling (e.g., Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks), including tuning them to a signal-to-noise ratio developers will tolerate.
* Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your development work today, have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't, and have built agentic workflows that other engineers adopted.
* Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build.

**Preferred Knowledge and Skills:**

* Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope.
* Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management — the platform you build is what produces that evidence.
* Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA).
* Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) — your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer.
* Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage — enough to know what the automation you build has to get right.
* Experience with threat modeling at a system level.

**About You:**

* You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better.
* You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it.
* You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
* You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things.
* You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
* You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
* You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting.

  You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
* You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

**Sezzle's Technology Stack:**

* **Frontend:** Typescript - React and React Native
* **Backend:** Golang
* **Database:** MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
* **DevOps & Cloud:** AWS, Kubernetes

* **CI/CD:** Gitlab
* **Testing:** Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests
* **Open Source:** Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!

**What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome?**

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. * Strong experience of **5-8+ years** in testing distributed systems and analyzing inter-service API behavior
* Hands-on experience with request payload tampering, fuzzing, or adversarial API testing techniques
* Understanding of layered defense architectures, including the distinction between synchronous/inline validation and asynchronous/background verification processes
* Familiarity with testing data persistence and relational/hierarchical integrity in backend data stores
* Demonstrated discipline in test log archival, evidence capture, and structured documentation practices
* Solid understanding of backend/middleware architecture, failure modes, and system boundaries
* Familiarity with API testing tools and scripting for building custom fuzzing/tampering test cases
